knowledge:
- key_parameters: ns=Minimum number of CpGs contained in each window for BSmooth (default 70) ;; h=Half the minimum window width for BSmooth (default 1000) ;; maxGap=The longest distance between two CpGs before a cluster is broken up (default 100000000 for BSmooth/BSmooth.tstat, 300bp for dmrFinder) ;; estimate.var=In BSmooth.tstat, specifies which samples are used to estimate variability (e.g., "group2" to use only control/normal samples, "same" for equal variability, or "paired" for a paired t-test) ;; local.correct=In BSmooth.tstat, logical indicating whether to use a large-scale (low-frequency) mean correction, which is highly recommended for cancer datasets ;; cutoff=In dmrFinder, the t-statistic thresholds used to identify candidate DMRs (e.g., c(-4.6, 4.6)) ;; qcutoff=In dmrFinder, quantile-based cutoffs (e.g., c(0.01, 0.99)) ;; BACKEND=In read.bismark, set to "HDF5Array" to enable HDF5-backed out-of-memory processing ;; BPPARAM=Parallelization backend configuration (e.g., MulticoreParam(workers = 10)) ;; parallelBy=In BSmooth, controls whether parallelization is performed over "sample" or "chromosome"
- alternatives: fisherTests=Can be used to perform Fisher's exact test for each locus individually, which is an alternative to the smoothing and t-statistic workflow ;; binomialGoodnessOfFit=Used to assess binomial model goodness of fit ;; poissonGoodnessOfFit=Used to assess Poisson model goodness of fit
- when_to_use: Appropriate for whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) or Oxford Nanopore sequencing data where CpG methylation is measured at base resolution across large genomic regions. It is best applied when biological replicates are available to estimate biological variation.
- pitfalls: running_tstats_without_filtering=Do not run BSmooth.tstat without filtering out low-coverage CpGs first, as this will lead to many false-positive DMRs in low-coverage regions ;; windows_compatibility=Parallel processing using mc.cores > 1 is not supported on MS Windows due to OS limitations ;; strand_collapse_errors=When combining strands manually, ensure that 1 is subtracted from the position of CpGs on the "-" strand to correctly align with the "+" strand ;; jagged_plots=Smoothed methylation profiles may appear jagged when plotted because they are only evaluated at actual CpG loci and linearly interpolated, rather than evaluated on a regular grid ;; memory_limits=Standard in-memory processing requires substantial RAM (e.g., ~32GB for parallel processing of 8 human samples); use the HDF5 backend for larger datasets

workflows.name: standard_wgbs_analysis
workflows.intent: Analyze WGBS data to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) using in-memory processing.
input: raw_alignment_summaries.txt (summarized evidence containing genomic positions, M/Methylation values, and Cov/Coverage values)
workflows.stages: 1. Instantiate and order the BSseq object ;; 2. Smooth the methylation profiles using BSmooth ;; 3. Filter out low-coverage loci ;; 4. Compute t-statistics with local correction ;; 5. Identify DMRs by thresholding t-statistics ;; 6. Plot individual or multiple DMRs
workflows.code:
library(bsseq)
library(bsseqData)

data(BS.cancer.ex)
BS.cancer.ex <- updateObject(BS.cancer.ex)
BS.cancer.ex
pData(BS.cancer.ex)

BS.cancer.ex.fit <- BSmooth(
    BSseq = BS.cancer.ex,
    BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(workers = 1),
    verbose = TRUE)

BS.cov <- getCoverage(BS.cancer.ex.fit)
keepLoci.ex <- which(rowSums(BS.cov[, BS.cancer.ex$Type == "cancer"] >= 2) >= 2 &
                     rowSums(BS.cov[, BS.cancer.ex$Type == "normal"] >= 2) >= 2)
BS.cancer.ex.fit <- BS.cancer.ex.fit[keepLoci.ex,]

BS.cancer.ex.tstat <- BSmooth.tstat(BS.cancer.ex.fit, 
                                    group1 = c("C1", "C2", "C3"),
                                    group2 = c("N1", "N2", "N3"), 
                                    estimate.var = "group2",
                                    local.correct = TRUE,
                                    verbose = TRUE)

plot(BS.cancer.ex.tstat)

dmrs0 <- dmrFinder(BS.cancer.ex.tstat, cutoff = c(-4.6, 4.6))
dmrs <- subset(dmrs0, n >= 3 & abs(meanDiff) >= 0.1)

pData <- pData(BS.cancer.ex.fit)
pData$col <- rep(c("red", "blue"), each = 3)
pData(BS.cancer.ex.fit) <- pData

plotRegion(BS.cancer.ex.fit, dmrs[1,], extend = 5000, addRegions = dmrs)

pdf(file = "dmrs_top200.pdf", width = 10, height = 5)
plotManyRegions(BS.cancer.ex.fit, dmrs[1:200,], extend = 5000,
                addRegions = dmrs)
dev.off()

workflows.name: large_scale_hdf5_analysis
workflows.intent: Process large-scale WGBS datasets using HDF5-backed objects to bound memory consumption.
workflows.stages: 1. Read Bismark files directly into an HDF5-backed BSseq object ;; 2. Alternatively, convert an existing in-memory BSseq object to HDF5 ;; 3. Load the HDF5-backed object ;; 4. Run parallelized smoothing with bounded memory
workflows.code:
library(HDF5Array)

BSseq <- read.bismark(bismarkfiles, BACKEND = "HDF5Array", BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(workers = 10))

saveHDF5SummarizedExperiment(BSseq, dir = "./BSseqName.h5")

BSseq <- loadHDF5SummarizedExperiment(dir = "./BSseqName.h5")

BSseq <- BSmooth(BSseq, BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(workers = 10))
